deliveryModel: 36 narrow module slices → six cumulative arc projects → M26 evidence-gated local capstone

projects.title: Stateful Atlas event ledger
projects.premise: Make a small event ledger explainable from binding to asymptotic cost.
projects.architecture: immutable event inputs → state transition functions → invariant checks → trace dossier
milestones: Name values, bindings, frames, representations, and contracts before implementation.
Add an abstract data type with a proof/cost note and a falsifying test.
Compare two implementations and defend the smallest design choice.
deliveryLoop: test, trace, numerical experiment, or proof check
code review, learner explanation, and evidence card

moduleSlices.title: Values, State, and Execution
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for bindings, object identity, mutation, and frame-local state.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you predict an aliasing or mutation trace before seeing the result, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: assignment copies an object or a function can only change its own local names
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: which behavior follows from Python's data model versus a CPython implementation detail
moduleSlices.transferTarget: debugging a shared configuration object without adding defensive copies blindly

moduleSlices.title: Functions, Recursion, and Induction
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a recursive contract joined to its base case, inductive step, and termination measure.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you reconstruct a recursive return trace and the corresponding induction argument, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a recursive call is justified merely because its input looks smaller
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: what fails when the measure does not decrease or the hypothesis is too weak
moduleSlices.transferTarget: choosing a safe recursive traversal for a tree-shaped input

moduleSlices.title: Abstraction, Interfaces, and Abstract Data Types
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for an abstract data type's behavioral contract separated from its representation invariant.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you read one operation and explain how it preserves the invariant without exposing internals, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: public fields and incidental representation details are automatically part of an API
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: when a representation swap is safe and when an observable behavior breaks substitution
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing an adapter around a storage implementation that may change later

moduleSlices.title: Logic, Sets, Relations, Graphs, and Proof
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for precise domains, quantifiers, relations, and proof obligations.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you repair a short proof or construct a countermodel for a nearby false statement, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: several examples, a diagram, or a true converse establishes a universal implication
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the exact hypothesis needed for the claim and the difference between a finite trace and a proof
moduleSlices.transferTarget: turning an informal program rule into a relation or invariant worth testing

moduleSlices.title: Cost Models and Algorithm Analysis
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a cost model with an asymptotic claim, constants, and an input family.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you derive a bound from counted operations and defend the model being counted, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: Big-O means approximately equal, or one benchmark establishes an asymptotic result
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: what a small timing observation cannot distinguish about two growth claims
moduleSlices.transferTarget: choosing a data representation for a workload with stated operations and limits

acceptanceCriteria: The learner states intent, constraints, and invariant before the patch or derivation.
Every generated patch, trace, or numerical result is visible and labelled as observed, simulated, assumed, or unverified.
At least one failure, counterexample, changed premise, or boundary is investigated.
The learner reviews the final artifact and explains the mechanism plus one remaining uncertainty.

projects.title: Indexed retrieval and route planner
projects.premise: Turn representation and algorithm choices into an inspectable retrieval system.
projects.architecture: records → sequence/index choices → priority/frontier structures → graph routes → measured trade-off
milestones: Trace one representation through memory, iteration, and update operations.
Add an index and route strategy with stated invariants and cost bounds.
Inject an adversarial input and explain why a different strategy wins or loses.
deliveryLoop: test, trace, numerical experiment, or proof check
code review, learner explanation, and evidence card

moduleSlices.title: Representation, Memory, Sequences, and Linked Structures
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for the relationship between sequence meaning, concrete storage, locality, and operation cost.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace a sequence operation through array or linked representation and its ownership changes, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: linked structures are inherently faster or memory representation is invisible to the API
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: which cost depends on access pattern, allocation, or implementation rather than the abstract ADT
moduleSlices.transferTarget: diagnosing an unexpected slow path in a queue-like service

moduleSlices.title: Stacks, Queues, Iteration, and Lazy Computation
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for restricted access, deferred computation, and the difference between producing and consuming work.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you predict iterator or generator state across a short pull sequence, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a lazy pipeline has already done its work or can be replayed without a new source
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: when laziness changes memory behavior but not a source's side effects or termination
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing a streaming ETL path for accidental repeated consumption

moduleSlices.title: Hashing, Dictionaries, Sets, and Indexing
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for equality, hashing, collision handling, and indexing under a workload.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace lookup or insertion while stating the equality and hash contract, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: hashes uniquely identify values or mutable keys are always safe
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the difference between expected lookup cost, adversarial behavior, and a correctness guarantee
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing an index for records whose identity rules may evolve

moduleSlices.title: Trees, Heaps, Sorting, and Ordered Search
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for ordered invariants in trees and heaps, plus the property a sorting/search procedure preserves.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you walk through one rotation, heap repair, or comparison sequence and state the invariant afterward, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a visually tree-shaped structure is ordered or a sorted output proves a stable/complete algorithm
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: which ordering property is required and what duplicates or comparator behavior change
moduleSlices.transferTarget: choosing an ordered structure for scheduling, nearest lookup, or ranked results

moduleSlices.title: Graph Algorithms and Network Models
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a graph model of vertices, edges, reachability, and the question an algorithm actually answers.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you predict a traversal or shortest-path state sequence from an edge list, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a path found by one traversal is automatically shortest, complete, or a flow solution
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: which edge weights, direction, and graph assumptions make the conclusion legal
moduleSlices.transferTarget: modeling a dependency, routing, or social-network question without confusing connection with causation

moduleSlices.title: Algorithm Design Paradigms: Choosing a Strategy from Structure
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for algorithm strategy chosen from structure, recurrence, exchange argument, or subproblem state.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you reconstruct why greedy, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, or search fits one problem, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a strategy that works on examples is justified or dynamic programming just means caching
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the structural property or counterexample that rules a tempting strategy in or out
moduleSlices.transferTarget: critiquing an AI-generated algorithm choice before implementation begins

acceptanceCriteria: The learner states intent, constraints, and invariant before the patch or derivation.
Every generated patch, trace, or numerical result is visible and labelled as observed, simulated, assumed, or unverified.
At least one failure, counterexample, changed premise, or boundary is investigated.
The learner reviews the final artifact and explains the mechanism plus one remaining uncertainty.

projects.title: Durable evidence service
projects.premise: Make a small service evolvable, testable, observable, serializable, and transactional.
projects.architecture: typed boundary → domain contract → tests/telemetry → serialized artifact → transactional store
milestones: Separate module/API direction from domain behavior and test seams.
Repair a seeded defect using an observable contract, not a blind patch.
Demonstrate one safe migration or transaction rollback and state the boundary.
deliveryLoop: test, trace, numerical experiment, or proof check
code review, learner explanation, and evidence card

moduleSlices.title: Modules, APIs, Types, and Dependency Direction
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for dependency direction, interface ownership, and what a module may know or call.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you read an import/API path and identify the contract crossing each boundary, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a type annotation or package boundary alone creates a stable architecture
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: what change would leak through the boundary and which dependency is owned by whom
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing a proposed integration without letting a UI concern invert the dependency graph

moduleSlices.title: Specifications, Testing, Debugging, and Observability
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a specification as an observable contract supported by tests, debugging, and scoped observation.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace a failing test to the claim it does and does not establish, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a green suite proves correctness or a debugger observation is the whole explanation
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the missing input, invariant, environment, or regression condition
moduleSlices.transferTarget: turning an incident report into a minimal reproducer and a lasting test

moduleSlices.title: Software Design and Change
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for design boundaries that make likely change explicit without over-abstracting the present system.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you compare two dependency designs and explain the change each makes cheap or risky, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: more layers, patterns, or classes automatically improve maintainability
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the actual volatility and evidence that justify a new abstraction
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing an AI-produced refactor for coupling, test seams, and reversibility

moduleSlices.title: Files, Serialization, Packaging, and Delivery
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a versioned artifact crossing a serialization, packaging, or delivery boundary.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace data from in-memory model through encoding, validation, and a consumer contract, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a successful parse proves compatibility or a package install proves reproducibility
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the version, schema, environment, and rollback assumptions behind a delivery claim
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing a backward-compatible change to a saved learner artifact

moduleSlices.title: Relational Data and Transactions
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for relational invariants, transaction boundaries, and concurrent changes to shared facts.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you walk through a failed or retried transaction and name the invariant at each durable step, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a database automatically prevents every race or an application retry is harmless
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the isolation, uniqueness, idempotency, and recovery assumptions needed for the claim
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing a small enrollment or progress-record update that tolerates retries

acceptanceCriteria: The learner states intent, constraints, and invariant before the patch or derivation.
Every generated patch, trace, or numerical result is visible and labelled as observed, simulated, assumed, or unverified.
At least one failure, counterexample, changed premise, or boundary is investigated.

projects.title: Failure-aware local protocol
projects.premise: Connect machine execution, resources, concurrency, protocols, partial failure, and trust.
projects.architecture: process boundary → resource ownership → concurrent actors → framed protocol → failure/authority ledger
milestones: Trace one request across stack, process, resource, and protocol boundaries.
Add concurrency or async behavior with a history and cancellation contract.
Threat-model one trust boundary and demonstrate a bounded failure recovery.
deliveryLoop: test, trace, numerical experiment, or proof check
code review, learner explanation, and evidence card

moduleSlices.title: Computer Architecture and the Execution Stack
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for the execution stack from source-level intent through machine-level representation and effects.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace one Python operation across frames, calls, memory, and CPU-level constraints, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: source syntax directly determines one universal machine behavior
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the difference between language semantics, a compiler/interpreter mechanism, and a hardware observation
moduleSlices.transferTarget: explaining why a performance or memory claim needs a named runtime and workload

moduleSlices.title: Operating Systems and Resource Mediation
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for operating-system mediation of processes, memory, files, interruption, and resource lifetime.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you read an interruption trace and identify which resource state is durable, recoverable, or unknown, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a process exit, API return, or file close alone proves a complete published result
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the ownership, flushing, and recovery evidence needed after failure
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing a safe staged write that can be inspected after a crash

moduleSlices.title: Concurrency and Parallelism
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for concurrent histories, ownership, progress guarantees, and the difference between possible and observed schedules.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you reconstruct a short interleaving and state the violated or preserved invariant, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a passing run rules out a race or parallelism is merely faster concurrency
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: what scheduling, visibility, and synchronization guarantees the reasoning needs
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing a worker-pool change for lost updates or stuck progress

moduleSlices.title: Networks and Application Protocols
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for an application protocol as a sequence of scoped messages, states, and durability claims.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace one request, response, retry, and timeout without inventing a remote fact, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a local send or HTTP success proves the receiver durably applied the intended effect
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the protocol version, idempotency, ordering, and failure assumptions
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing a reliable client-visible status for a delayed remote operation

moduleSlices.title: Async and Distributed Systems
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for partial failure, async coordination, and recovery without pretending a distributed system has global certainty.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you walk through an event attempt and separate local completion, remote observation, and durable effect, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: retries guarantee delivery exactly once or an awaited call made the whole workflow atomic
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the retry, ordering, timeout, and compensation assumptions behind the result
moduleSlices.transferTarget: choosing a bounded fallback when an external dependency becomes unavailable

moduleSlices.title: Security, Privacy & Trust Boundaries
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for trust boundaries among data, identity, authority, provenance, privacy, and human control.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you follow one sensitive action through its actor, capability, data recipient, and audit evidence, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: authentication, encryption, or a trusted vendor automatically establishes authorization and safety
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: who may act, what is retained, what is reversible, and what evidence is still missing
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing an agent proposal that requests a new tool or private data source

projects.architecture: bounded language input → interpreter/runtime evidence → retrieval/claim ledger → human-facing decision surface

Profile a narrow path and attach evidence to an intelligent-system claim.
Prepare the M26 capstone architecture defense and open-source stewardship plan.

moduleSlices.title: Programming Languages, Interpreters & Bounded Evaluation
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for the separation of text, syntax tree, evaluation, type/capability boundary, and authority.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you parse and evaluate a small expression while naming the permitted language and environment, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: parsing validates safety or restricting syntax automatically controls capabilities
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the language, evaluation, resource, and authority limits that must be independently enforced
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing a bounded rule language for a learner-facing automation

moduleSlices.title: CPython, Performance & Memory Evidence
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for the boundary between a Python guarantee, CPython mechanism, and scoped benchmark observation.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you read a measurement and reconstruct its workload, runtime, baseline, and limitation, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: one benchmark or profiler output proves a portable performance claim
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: which version, allocator, workload, hardware, and statistical limits prevent generalization
moduleSlices.transferTarget: reviewing an optimization proposal before approving it for the course portal

moduleSlices.title: Evidence-Grounded Intelligent & Human-Centered Systems
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for an evidence-grounded decision that keeps model output, authority, uncertainty, and human control distinct.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace one suggestion from input through model/evidence, display policy, and a reversible human decision, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a high score, agent explanation, or green evaluation creates permission to act
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the data lineage, evaluation scope, owner, consent, and rollback evidence needed for release
moduleSlices.transferTarget: writing a bounded AI-assisted feature contract with a meaningful refusal or correction path

moduleSlices.title: Systems Capstone, Open-Source Stewardship & Oral Architecture Defense
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a release argument joining architecture, invariant, test/observation, human impact, limitation, and rollback.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you defend one architecture thread while a reviewer changes a premise or removes an evidence source, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a polished demo, CI pass, or agent-generated dossier is a release decision
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the owner, recovery path, uncertainty, and changed constraint that should narrow, defer, or disable the release
moduleSlices.transferTarget: handing the system to a maintainer who did not build it and can still challenge its claims

projects.architecture: formal object → numerical/algorithmic experiment → assumption ledger → learning claim → reliability boundary
milestones: Derive a discrete, linear, continuous, probabilistic, and optimization claim with hypotheses.

moduleSlices.title: Discrete Mathematics, Proof, Counting & Structures
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for definitions, quantifiers, induction/invariants, counting structure, and a minimal counterexample.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you reconstruct a proof or recurrence argument, then distinguish it from a finite Python trace, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: examples prove universals or a recurrence is complete without bases and a domain
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the missing quantifier, base case, invariant, or hypothesis that makes a claim false
moduleSlices.transferTarget: using proof structure to audit a graph, scheduling, or AI-generated correctness claim

moduleSlices.title: Linear Algebra, Numerical Stability & Representation
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for linear maps, projections, rank, spectra, and conditioning as a model of representable information.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you derive least squares, a projection, or PCA from its assumptions, then audit one shape/dtype/solver path and finite-precision boundary, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a matrix formula automatically yields a stable computation or PCA is merely an API call
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the conditioning, scale, rank, and approximation assumptions behind the numerical result
moduleSlices.transferTarget: critiquing a representation-reduction choice in an ML or scientific workflow

moduleSlices.title: Calculus, Real Analysis & Continuous Change
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for a continuous-change claim joining domain/metric, local map or accumulation, and a named convergence or numerical-error condition.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you derive a limit/Taylor/Jacobian/change-of-variables or convergence step, then audit one shape, unit, dtype, step, tolerance, or solver trace, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a pointwise limit is automatically uniform, a partial derivative proves differentiability, or a finite numerical trace licenses an operation exchange
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the continuity, differentiability, region/injectivity, convergence, regularity, and finite-precision assumptions that can fail
moduleSlices.transferTarget: deciding whether a scientific simulation, optimization update, or expectation manipulation is justified in a new model

moduleSlices.title: Probability, Statistics & Scientific Inference
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for probability models, conditional structure, inference, uncertainty, and sampling assumptions.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you derive a Bayes, likelihood, confidence, or concentration argument before simulating it, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: a p-value, interval, posterior, or Monte Carlo output answers a stronger question than its model permits
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the sampling, independence, missingness, misspecification, and multiple-testing assumptions
moduleSlices.transferTarget: designing an experiment or model evaluation with a credible uncertainty statement

moduleSlices.title: Optimization & Information
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for an objective, constraints, geometry, convergence path, and information quantity with assumptions.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you derive a first-order/KKT or entropy/KL step and connect it to a computational consequence, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: an optimizer's decrease proves a good solution or information metrics are interchangeable scores
moduleSlices.boundaryToName: the convexity, smoothness, feasibility, scale, and numerical assumptions behind a convergence claim
moduleSlices.transferTarget: choosing a loss, constraint, or stopping rule for an evidence-bearing system

moduleSlices.title: Systems Languages, Scientific Python & Accelerators

moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you trace one scientific Python operation through memory layout, kernel work, precision, and reproducibility evidence, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.

moduleSlices.title: Formal Languages, Computability & Complexity
moduleSlices.scope: One bounded implementation, trace, proof, or experiment for language recognition, computation models, reductions, and the boundary between solvable, efficient, and approximable.
moduleSlices.learnerArtifact: A reviewed artifact in which you classify a small language or reconstruct a reduction while preserving the yes/no relationship, with one assumption, one changed-premise result, and one non-claim.
moduleSlices.misconceptionToRepair: NP means impossible, a parser solves every language question, or a hard instance proves a class claim

moduleSlices.title: Classical AI: Search, Constraints & Decision

definitionOfDone: A reviewable architecture and data-flow map connects the arc outputs.
The learner can trace one claim from source or experiment to a bounded user-facing decision.
Privacy, accessibility, safety, provenance, and failure boundaries are explicit.
The learner conducts a constructive oral architecture defense and records uncertainty without a pass/fail label.
